title: Maximum Building Height
summary: Construct a sequence of n buildings with heights adhering to specific constraints: the first building must be at height 0, each subsequent building's height can differ by at most 1 from its neighbor, and certain buildings must not exceed given maximum heights.
statement: Construct a sequence of n buildings with heights adhering to specific constraints: the first building must be at height 0, each subsequent building's height can differ by at most 1 from its neighbor, and certain buildings must not exceed given maximum heights. The task is to determine the tallest possible building height under these conditions.
constraints: Building one has height zero; adjacent nonnegative heights differ by at most one.
Each [index,max_height] is an upper bound; return the greatest achievable height anywhere.
hints: Restrictions constrain each other through the adjacent slope limit.
Add [1,0], sort, then tighten heights left-to-right and right-to-left.
Between consecutive feasible endpoints, the highest peak is floor((left_height+right_height+distance)/2).
The two passes compute tight endpoint caps; rising from both ends at slope one meets at that formula, giving both an upper bound and a constructible peak.

tests.explanation: The restrictions allow a peak of two at building five.
Without additional restrictions, heights can rise from zero to five.
